document.title: Post-Conference Comments of The Dayton Power and Light Company d/b/a AES Ohio re PJM Governance and Stakeholder Reforms
document.group: PJM governance and stakeholder reform vote
document.filer: Dayton Power and Light Company, The

pages.text:
UNITED STATES OF AMERICA  
FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION 
 
 
POST-CONFERENCE COMMENTS OF  
THE DAYTON POWER AND LIGHT COMPANY D/B/A AES OHIO 
 
(July 30, 2026) 
 
The Dayton Power and Light Company d/b/a AES Ohio (“AES Ohio”) hereby 
submits the following post-conference comments in response to the Notice Requesting 
Post-Conference Comment issued on July 30, 2026 by the Federal Energy Regulatory 
Commission (“Commission”), including the issues list included in the appendix of the 
notice. 
 
PJM Board Independence 
 
 
Questions/Comments 
Yes 
No
1) 
Should Board members’ terms be extended to five or more years? 
x 
 
 
Comments: Board members’ terms should be extended to five years or more 
(subject to limited removal provisions (e.g., serious misconduct)) to allow for 
longer-term, independent decision making. 
2) 
Should there be a maximum number of years that a Board member 
may serve (e.g., 10 years)? 
x 
 
 
Comments: Yes, see response to No. 1. 
3) 
Should the Board member qualification rules be revised to provide a 
preference for some Board members that reside in the PJM region? 
 
x 
 
Comments: No, Board members should be selected from the best candidates 
available regardless of residence.  Some of the best candidates reside outside of 
the PJM region, including some with international experience, and the Board 
PJM Governance and Stakeholder Reforms 
Docket No. AD26-7-000

Questions/Comments 
Yes 
No
should be composed of individuals with experience both within and outside of 
PJM to ensure different perspectives are included on the Board. 
4) 
Should the conflict-of-interest rules be revised to reduce the cooling 
off period for Board members from two years to one year? 
x 
 
 
Comments: Yes, the conflict-of-interest rules should be revised to reduce the 
cooling off period for Board members from two years to one year to ensure that 
the most qualified candidates are considered. 
5) 
Should restrictions on Board communications be relaxed to enable 
more communication between the Board and stakeholders? 
x 
 
 
Comments: Yes, restrictions on Board communications should be relaxed to 
enable more communication between the Board and stakeholders, such as the 
communication permitted by other RTOs. 
6) 
In order to increase transparency, should Board votes be made public 
or the Board be required to explain its reasoning?  
X 
(in 
part)
 
 
Comments: Board votes should not be made public to foster Board independence 
However, the Board should be required to explain its reasoning for the votes it 
has made to provide transparency. 
7) 
In order to increase transparency, should some Board meetings be 
open or available to the public? 
x 
 
 
Comments: Yes, it is appropriate for some Board meetings be open or available to 
the public to provide a level of transparency, but there may be other meetings that 
should not be open. 
8) 
Should PJM’s governing documents be revised to explicitly state that 
the responsibility of PJM and its Board is to serve the public interest? 
 
x 
 
Comments: No, PJM’s governing documents be revised to explicitly state that the 
responsibility of PJM and its Board is to serve the public interest. 
9) 
Should state representatives have at least one voting member on the 
Nominating Committee? 
x 
 
 
Comments: Yes, state representatives should have at least one voting member on 
the Nominating Committee.  Currenltly, the nominating process is robust and

Questions/Comments 
Yes 
No
professional.  State representative participation would provide transparency to the 
states that the best candidates for the Board are being considered and selected.   
10)
Should PJM adopt public performance metrics and tie management 
compensation to their achievement? 
 
x 
 
Comments: No, PJM should not adopt public performance metrics and tie 
management compensation to their achievement.  Metrics for PJM’s performance 
would be difficult to design well and could lead to improper incentives for its 
management. 
 
Section 205 Filing Rights 
 
 
Questions/Comments 
Yes
No
11) 
Should the stakeholder process be advisory, i.e., stakeholder votes 
only inform the Board? 
x 
 
 
Comments: Yes, the stakeholder process should be advisory.  Stakeholder input 
is important, but members currently exercise undue influence over PJM.  PJM 
should have the right to make filings at FERC that it believes are necessary to 
ensure reliability and run efficient wholesale markets without requiring 
stakeholder agreement.  Members would continue to have all of their rights at 
FERC. 
12) 
Should PJM have section 205 filing rights over the energy market and 
ancillary services unencumbered by the requirement to obtain 
approval of two-thirds of the Members Committee? 
x 
 
 
Comments: Yes, see above.   
13) 
Should PJM have section 205 filing rights over Regional 
Transmission Expansion Planning (RTEP) unencumbered by the 
requirement to obtain approval of two-thirds of the Members 
Committee? 
x 
 
 
Comments: Yes, see above.   
14) 
Should the Organization of PJM States Inc (OPSI) have “jump ball” 
rights over resource adequacy and transmission cost allocation filings 
when a supermajority of OPSI agrees on an alternative proposal? 
 
x

Questions/Comments 
Yes
No
 
Comments: No.  These rights belong to PJM Transmission Owners. 
15) 
Should the Members Committee have “jump ball” filing rights over 
the portions of the tariff where PJM has 205 filing rights when a 
supermajority of stakeholders approves an alternative proposal? 
 
x 
 
Comments: No.  Stakeholder input (including the level of support from 
stakeholders) should be considered by PJM when making decisions. 
 
Stakeholder Process 
 
 
Questions/Comments 
Yes
No
16) 
Should the approval threshold in the Members Committee be lowered 
from two-thirds sector-weighted voting? 
 
x 
 
Comments: No, the approval threshold in the Members Committee should not be 
lowered from two-thirds sector-weighted voting.  The current sector weighting 
appropriate balances sectors; However, reform is necessary associated with 
members’ use of agency voting, which typically results in just a handful of agents 
casting votes for more than 50% of the votes cast. 
17) 
Should the voting rules barring affiliate votes, which apply to senior 
standing committees, also apply to lower-level committees? 
 
x 
 
Comments: No, the current rules balance upper and lower committees and 
appropriately recognize member size in the market.  A member’s financial 
commitment to PJM should be reflected.  In past, other reforms that 
acknowledged these differences between members were explored, but rejected, 
and thus, the rules should be preserved here. 
 
State Participation 
 
 
Questions/Comments 
Yes
No
18) 
In addition to OPSI, should there be a second state representative 
group consisting of governors’ representatives and/or state legislators’ 
representatives? 
 
x 
 
Comments: No, OPSI appropriately represents states and additional groups could

Questions/Comments 
Yes
No
cause unnecessary confusion regarding the positions of the states.  However, the 
invitation list should be expanded to include States in the existing OPSI 
meetings.   
19) 
Should state representatives have a formal voting role in the 
stakeholder process (limited to certain topics, such as resource 
adequacy and regional transmission cost allocation) in addition to the 
consumer advocate votes?   
 
x 
 
Comments: No, providing state representatives with a formal voting role in the 
stakeholder process could create situations where state representatives are voting 
on actions that they must later review in state processes.  
 
20) 
Should PJM be required to consult with OPSI prior to making section 
205 filing related to resource adequacy and transmission cost 
allocation? 
 
x 
 
Comments: No.  By agreement and by law, Transmission Owners have the right 
to make such Section 205 filings, and there is an existing process at FERC for 
their review and OPSI comment. 
 
Respectfully submitted,
